reason: Rain can absorb atmospheric carbon dioxide, providing a plausible starting point for weathering basalt.
expectation: The water will take up carbon dioxide and become mildly acidic.

effect: The rain is mildly acidic and can now help weather susceptible minerals in the basalt.
reaction: The result confirms the expected first step toward chemical weathering.
reason: Acidic rain can react with the young basaltic crust, starting the transfer of dissolved material.
expectation: The rain will weather minerals in the basalt and release dissolved material.

effect: The basalt is changing under water and releasing dissolved constituents, which runoff may carry toward the sea.
reaction: The result clarifies that weathering can occur without biological soil.
reason: Runoff is the visible route for moving weathered material toward the basin.
expectation: Runoff will carry dissolved constituents away from the altered basalt.

effect: Runoff now carries dissolved ions from the weathered basalt, ready to enter the sea.
reaction: It is striking that clear-looking water can carry material from rock.
reason: The accumulating sea is the destination for the dissolved material in runoff.
expectation: The runoff will deliver dissolved ions to the sea.

effect: Dissolved minerals have reached the sea, completing the first goal; fine sediment remains.
reaction: The distinction between dissolved minerals and a ready-made supply of salt is useful.
reason: The altered basalt is a plausible source of sediment, but its next available partner is not clear.
expectation: The inspection will show whether the altered basalt can produce material for sediment.

alternatives.reason: Runoff might also reveal a way to transport sediment.

effect: The inspection automatically produced fine solid particles, a separate pathway from dissolved ions toward sediment.
reaction: The contrast between transported particles and dissolved material is useful.
reason: Runoff can carry the loosened particles toward the basin.
expectation: The runoff will transport the fine particles toward the sea.

alternatives.reason: The particles might settle directly in sheltered water, but transport seems likely to come first.

effect: The fine particles are suspended in runoff and can now be deposited where the water slows.
reaction: The distinction between cloudy suspended solids and dissolved material is clear.
reason: Sheltered water should slow the flow and let suspended sediment settle.
expectation: Fine particles will settle out and form sediment.

effect: The suspended particles settled in sheltered water, completing the sediment goal and the chapter.
reaction: It was satisfying to see the transported particles become a sediment bed.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following weathered rock into dissolved ions and then solid sediment was worthwhile because it showed two distinct ways water transports material.

leastWorthwhile.text: The delivery of dissolved material to the sea was a predictable step once the runoff carried it, though it completed the first goal.

surprise.text: The inspection automatically combined the altered basalt with rain to make fine particles, revealing a separate solid-particle pathway.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt particularly arbitrary; inspecting the altered basalt was useful because its next partner was not obvious.

continue.text: Yes. I would continue to see how the sea and its surroundings change, especially after the clear distinction between dissolved and suspended material.
